chunk_map.heading: Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every pronoun/demonstrative under the sequential-read bar against the current (2026-08-29 compaction) body. Chunk 1 line 5: "the agent has no say in whether it runs" -> "it" = "hook", same sentence; "whether or not the model remembers it exists" -> "it" = "the script", same sentence. Chunk 2 line 10: "Anything that breaks the work if it skips belongs in a hook" -> "it" = "Anything", same clause. Chunk 2 line 11: "The same primitive covers everything else" -> "primitive" resolves to "hook" named one sentence earlier in the same bullet. Closest call: line 15's closer "A menu, not a checklist." has no explicit antecedent noun, but its referent (the list of hooks the prompt at line 13 asks Claude to produce) is named one line above inside the SAME chunk ("Name the top five hooks..."), so it resolves as an immediate same-chunk continuation, not a never-named or forward-pointing referent. grep -inE 'you (did|saw|wrote|built|ran|caught|made)' over the body -> 0 hits, so no dangling backward-reference either.

grep -inE 'the opening lecture|earlier|previously|prior lecture|the last (lecture|module|slide)|that (lecture|module)' over body lines 1-16 -> 0 hits. Body contains no reference to another file, lecture, or module by position; the only file-level relationships (extraction from what-packaging-is.md, placement in learn-from-the-test.md) live below the maintainer cut (line 17+), out of the rendered slide body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'you (did|saw|wrote|built|ran|caught|made)' over body lines 1-16 -> 0 hits. No "the X you did/saw" construction naming a completed exercise beat anywhere in the current body -- nothing for this rule to strand.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'guess|predict|before you (watch|see|run)' over body lines 1-16 -> 0 hits. The 2026-08-29 compaction removed the last stage direction ("This one runs on the screen. Watch the list come back rather than typing along"); the remaining prompt is a plain trainer-run demo with no guess-then-reveal structure for a reveal to land ahead of.

Chunk 0 (lines 1-2) is the file's title-only slide (H1, no lede before the first ##) -- the standard title-slide shape across the corpus, not a wait-state fragment. Chunk 1 (lines 3-7) carries two full bullets (definition+mechanism at line 5, forgetfulness rationale at line 6). Chunk 2 (lines 8-16), even after the compaction pass cut it from four bullets to two, still carries two bullets, a live prompt, and a closing test line -- none of the three chunks reduces to a single wait-state fragment.

Chunk 1 header "Hooks always fire" (line 3) is proven by its own content: line 5's "whether or not the model remembers it exists" and line 6's "Hooks don't forget." Chunk 2 header "Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste" (line 8) is proven by lines 10-11's must-happen->hook / taste-shaped->prompt split. Closest call: closing line 15, "A menu, not a checklist" -- extends into which specific hooks are worth adopting, a corollary of the header's taste/prompt half, not a contradiction of it.

Checked every sub-item against the current body. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.': grep -inE '^\s*(-\s*)?Not [A-Za-z]' -> 0 hits. Anaphora/epistrophe triples: none (no three-part repeated sentence-opener). Self-grading superlatives: grep -inE 'one of the most|most useful|most powerful|most important' -> 0 hits; "A menu, not a checklist" does not grade the material's value. Number + own retraction: the only cardinal, "top five hooks" inside the prompt instruction, is a target count for the exercise's output, not a measurement the body hedges or retracts. Abstraction-noun stacks: none -- vocabulary stays concrete (verifier, pre-commit guard, session-start context loader). Empty-leg verb triplets: none present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|Connections|\bsurface\b' over body lines 1-16 -> 0 hits. "fires" (lines 5, 6) is the platform's own vocabulary for hook execution, confirmed by this file's own backing block whose cc-hooks-docs source [checked:2026-08-28] quotes hook events that "fire on every named event" -- not authorial repo dialect; an engineer reading Anthropic's hooks docs meets the identical word. "primitive", "verifier", "pre-commit guard", "session-start context loader" are ordinary engineering terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n '\*\*' over body -> 2 hits: line 5 "A **hook**" (1-word handle, first-mention coinage) and line 10 "**Must happen goes in a hook**" (closest call: 6 words, a paired-law maxim mirroring chunk 2's own header). Checked both budget clauses separately: (a) count -- this is the ONLY bold in chunk 2 (bullet 2 and the closer carry none, and the fixed "**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*" widget-frame label is not chunk body prose), so the <=1-per-slide budget holds; (b) content -- rule 9 explicitly permits "a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law," and chunk 2's entire job, per its own header, is stating exactly one law (must-happen->hook / recommended->prompt) -- the bolded clause is that law's handle, not a decorative whole-sentence lead competing with other emphasis. No dilution harm (the harm this rule exists to prevent) is present anywhere on this slide.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Pure lecture file, no runtime forks. Chunk 1 header "Hooks always fire" (line 3) and chunk 2 header "Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste" (line 8) are both full declarative claims about platform behavior, not topic labels or imperatives -- matches the lecture heading-grammar requirement.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1's two bullets: definition+mechanism (line 5) then the forgetfulness rationale (line 6) -- distinct content, no restatement. Chunk 2's two bullets, re-read fresh against the 2026-08-29 compaction: bullet 1 (line 10) states the must-happen/hook vs taste/prompt split with concrete hook examples; bullet 2 (line 11) narrows to the verifier example and generalizes it into "the same primitive covers everything else" -- the bridge into the demo prompt's five-hooks task, not a doctrine re-announcement, since bullet 1 never itself generalizes the verifier case. No self-referential design commentary (class b) anywhere. Closer (line 15) "A menu, not a checklist" is not a koan restating the header or a `**The point:**` line (class c) -- the maintainer block names it as the load-bearing new content that tells the room how to read the prompt's just-returned list, introducing information (menu vs. checklist) that neither the header nor bullet 1 stated.
